svg.text: In five short bullet points: when is a git worktree a better choice than switching
You can keep a long-running task (build, test suite,
review) going in one worktree while you work in another, with no stashing or WIP commits.
A hotfix or PR review can happen in a separate directory, so your
Each worktree keeps its own build artifacts and
avoid re-installing or recompiling every time you switch.
Comparing or testing side by side:
You can run two versions of the code at once, or diff
behavior between branches, without switching back and forth.
Each agent gets an isolated checkout, so they can't
clobber each other's files, though they all share one
